text:
anya: Heads-up — we started seeing token-tail lat spikes for /v1/generate (chat-prod) around 1967600000. Average P95 up ~120ms, P99 up ~400ms. Noticed SM occupancy drops on a subset of requests.
ryan: Seen it too. Any kernel-selector logs? Could be falling back to fallback kernels for seq>512 in the new selector change.
anya: I pulled a sample trace: `kernel_selector -> fallback: true, reason=missing_fastpath, seq_len=640, batch_size=1`
marta: Oof. That matches the timeframe of the batching-heuristic tweak we rolled yesterday (lowered target batch latency from 8ms -> 6ms). Might be creating smaller batches and exposing slow paths.
perf-bot: Profiling snapshot (1967654400): median SM occupancy down 18%, VRAM headroom increased ~300MB, but token-latency tail increased. Kernel wall time for attention kernel_v2 increased 2.3x on fallback. Link: https://dash.redwood.internal/p/abc123 (perf-snapshot-1967654400)
lee: Can someone paste the batcher config we deployed?
anya: Config excerpt: ```json
{"target_batch_latency_ms":6,"max_batch_size":64,"kv_cache_prefetch":true,"prefer_fast_kernels":true}
```
ryan: prefer_fast_kernels toggle may be mis-evaluating architecture constraints. If it favors smaller, specialized kernels they may not be compatible with quantized kernels, so selector picks generic kernel that is slower.
marta: Action: add token-level breakdown panel (per-route) showing prefetch hit/miss, kernel variant chosen, batch size distribution. Right now dashboards only show aggregate token latency + SM occupancy.
anya: I spun up a nvprof run on a straggler request. nvprof shows lots of small kernel launches and non-coalesced memory ops during KV prefetch phase. Suspect prefetch is thrashing L2 and causing SM underutilization.
perf-bot: Collected trace IDs: [tid-79a, tid-79b, tid-79c]. Lightweight flame: attention_kernel_generic (60%), kv_prefetch (25%), kernel_dispatch (10%), memcpy (5%).
lee: Good catch. If kv_prefetch runs on CPU thread and issues many small GPU memcpy ops, that could starve SMs. Can we move prefetch batching to the continuous-batcher thread?
ryan: Quick experiment idea: revert target_batch_latency to 8ms for chat-prod and measure P99 over 1h. Also add a metric for kernel_variant per token: `kernel.variant` tag.
marta: I'll add a dashboard draft: panels = [per-route token-latency breakdown by kernel.variant, batch size histogram, kv_prefetch hit ratio, SM occupancy heatmap across MIG slices, VRAM used by model shard, GPU power/thermal].
anya: Also we should surface an alert: if SM occupancy drops >15% while P99 token latency increases >50% for 5m, page eng-runtime oncall.
perf-bot: I pushed a quick profiling agent to collect kernel selector decisions for 1% of traffic for next 30m. Endpoint: /internal/profiler/kernel-decision?sample=0.01
lee: Who owns the kernel selector code to triage selector heuristic logic? @ryan?
ryan: I'll take a look. Plan: 1) roll back batcher tweak to 8ms on canary, 2) enable kernel.variant tagging in telemetry, 3) run 1% sampled kernel-decision traces, 4) evaluate moving kv_prefetch into batcher thread.
marta: Assigning tasks: ryan -> selector logs + rollback canary, anya -> collect nvprof traces + examine memcpy patterns, me (marta) -> dashboard panels + alert, lee -> experiment to move prefetch.
anya: I'll attach raw nvprof snippets in this thread when ready. Early note: memcpy bursts correlated with fallback kernel decisions.
ryan: Thanks — if rollback fixes it we'll then work on making selector more robust for quantized kernels.
marta: Sounds good. Updating the runbook. :thumbsup: 
anya: ping me once rollback is live and I'll re-run the straggler traces.
perf-bot: Incident marker created: perf-1967654321, severity=warning. Collected snapshots stored at s3://perf-traces/1967654321/
lee: moving to implement experiments. Will post results in ~45m.
anya: Thanks everyone.
